segments.t: DE
Session journalKTPH000

The session journal documents a terminal session as a readable timeline: every server output line and every command you type is written to a capture log, an AI periodically condenses the activity into short journal entries, and the result is rendered as a self-contained HTML page with connection details, color-coded excerpts, screenshots and your own notes. Journals are managed like saved chats — in their own manager window with search, editing and export.
KTPH000
Storage and formatsKTPH000
Each journal is one self-contained directory under KTPH000 (configurable in KTPH001Settings KTPH003 Logging KTPH004 Session JournalKTPH002):
File
Purpose
KTPH000
The curated journal document: metadata, AI summaries, markers, notes, screenshot references
KTPH000 / KTPH001 / KTPH002
The append-only capture log — timestamped server output and typed input lines with sequence ids
KTPH000, …
Rotated log parts; closed parts are zstd-compressed automatically, the journal never deletes history. Journals recorded by older versions keep their KTPH000 parts and remain fully readable
KTPH000
The generated timeline page, regenerated automatically after every change
KTPH000
Screenshots you attached during the session

The capture-log format is selectable in the journal manager's KTPH006OptionsKTPH007 dialog: KTPH008JSONKTPH009 (JSON Lines, the default), KTPH010XMLKTPH011 or KTPH012YAMLKTPH013. All formats carry the same fields, and every entry is exactly one line, so a crash never corrupts more than the last line. JSON is the default because log tooling reads it without needing a parser of its own — not because it saves space. Size barely separates the three: for ordinary output XML is about 9 bytes per entry smaller, for output full of KTPH000, KTPH001 and KTPH002 JSON is roughly 10 % smaller (XML has to escape those, JSON does not), and once a finished part is compressed all three land within 2 % of each other. YAML is the largest, since it writes JSON mappings with a KTPH003 prefix. The active log part stays uncompressed for live reads; rotation (default 25 MB per part) and session end compress finished parts to KTPH004 (zstd — journals from older versions keep their KTPH005 parts and open exactly as before).

Two more things keep long, noisy sessions small and complete. Consecutive identical output lines (progress loops, KTPH000 repeats) are coalesced syslog-style: the first occurrence is written immediately, follow-ups are counted and stored as one entry with a repeat count. The viewer shows such a run compactly as KTPH001, while copying or exporting the log reproduces the original lines in full. And when server output arrives faster than the log can persist it, the capture applies backpressure instead of dropping lines — the terminal may briefly slow down under an extreme flood, but the journal stays complete.

Rotation is configurable per connection on the KTPH001JournalKTPH002 tab: KTPH003Maximum size per log part (MB)KTPH004 (default 25) and KTPH005Maximum rotated log partsKTPH006 (default 20). After the configured number of parts, output capture stops with a note in the journal; input, screenshots and notes continue. An enterprise policy can cap the part count via KTPH000.
Enabling the journalKTPH000
Automatically for a connectionKTPH000
Open KTPH000Connections KTPH002 Manage ConnectionsKTPH001 and edit a connection
On the KTPH000JournalKTPH001 tab, enable KTPH002Enable session journal for this connectionKTPH003

Optionally adjust KTPH000Capture typed input linesKTPH001, KTPH002Generate AI summariesKTPH003, the per-connection KTPH004Summary intervalKTPH005, and the rotation pair KTPH006Maximum size per log part (MB)KTPH007 and KTPH008Maximum rotated log partsKTPH009
Every future connection of this server then starts its journal automatically. The journal survives reconnects and records a reconnect marker in the log.
Retroactively for a running sessionKTPH000

Use KTPH003Tools KTPH015 Start/Stop Session JournalKTPH004 (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010), the tab context menu (KTPH011Session Journal KTPH016 Start journalKTPH012) or the journal bar's KTPH013Start journalKTPH014 button. The existing scrollback is imported into the journal as seed entries first, so the timeline covers what already happened, then live capture attaches.

These controls open KTPH000Journal terminals…KTPH001. Check any open terminals or choose KTPH002All terminals in this tabKTPH003 to include the current terminals and splits you open later. Choose KTPH004ApplyKTPH005 to start one shared journal for the selection. Reopen the dialog to change the selection. A removed terminal stops contributing immediately, and its existing history stays in the journal. Clearing all selections ends the journal. Closing the last recorded terminal or closing the tab also ends it.

The shared journal puts each terminal's scrollback, input and output into one capture log with a label for the source terminal. The journal uses the first selected terminal's connection settings for rotation and AI summaries. Each terminal uses its own KTPH000Capture typed input linesKTPH001 setting. When several terminals contribute activity, summaries use bounded chronological excerpts with terminal labels.
AI connection test before the journal startsKTPH000

A journal whose summaries can never be written is of little use, so when the journal would call the AI (summaries switched on globally and for the connection, and allowed by policy), korTTY first checks that the AI profile answers. A successful test is remembered for ten minutes per profile, so opening further tabs does not ask the provider again.

KTPH003Starting the journal by handKTPH004 — the journal bar, the tab menu or KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 — shows KTPH011Testing the AI connection…KTPH012 and starts the journal only after the test passed. Output printed meanwhile is not lost: the scrollback is imported when the journal starts. If the test fails, a dialog names the profile and the reason (for example a missing API key or a refused connection) and offers KTPH013Test againKTPH014, KTPH015Record without AIKTPH016 — the journal records raw activity and can be KTPH017evaluated laterKTPH018 — or KTPH019CancelKTPH020.

KTPH000Journals that start automatically on connectKTPH001 begin capturing right away, so the terminal is never blocked; the test runs in the background. If it fails, a red bar below the terminal shows the profile and the reason, with KTPH002Test againKTPH003, KTPH004Record without AIKTPH005 and KTPH006End journalKTPH007.

KTPH000Automation runsKTPH001 test the AI once per run before their closing pass. If it does not answer, the run is kept as a log only and a timeline entry KTPH002AI not reachableKTPH003 says why — evaluate it later from the journal manager.
The journal barKTPH000

The bar below the terminal shows the focused terminal’s recording state and offers KTPH000Stop journalKTPH001 or, in a split tab, KTPH002Journal terminals…KTPH003. When the focused terminal is recording, the bar also offers KTPH004ScreenshotKTPH005 and KTPH006NoteKTPH007.

KTPH003ScreenshotKTPH004 (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010, also KTPH011Tools KTPH013 Add Journal ScreenshotKTPH012 and the terminal's right-click menu) captures the focused terminal and files it into the journal timeline. From the terminal’s right-click menu it captures the pane under the cursor.
KTPH000NoteKTPH001 opens the KTPH002note editorKTPH003 for a free-text remark that appears as its own timeline entry at the current position.

After stopping a journal, right-click KTPH003Start journalKTPH004 or the bar and choose KTPH005Hide journal barKTPH006 to hide it in that tab. Start a journal from the tab context menu or with KTPH007KTPH000KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH001KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH002KTPH012 to bring the bar back.
Writing notesKTPH000

Notes are written in the same editor everywhere they are edited — the journal bar's KTPH000NoteKTPH001 button, the live panel's, the entry form in the KTPH002viewerKTPH003, and the KTPH004screenshot editorKTPH005:
The field holds KTPH000at least six linesKTPH001 and the dialog can be resized, so a note can be a paragraph instead of a single line.

KTPH005Links are clickable.KTPH006 Any KTPH000 or KTPH001 address in a note becomes a link on the journal page — click it and the address opens in your system browser, never inside the journal view. Only those two schemes ever become links. Web addresses in AI summaries (KTPH002 or a bare KTPH003 host, never a file name) are clickable too — the summarizer has already dropped every statement naming a host the session does not show; terminal excerpts stay literal. Typed input is captured only as complete submitted lines, and several layers keep passwords out of the journal:

When the server output ends in a password prompt (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, and localized variants), the next submitted input line is suppressed and logged as a redacted placeholder — the typed text is never buffered or written.
The connection's own stored password is additionally replaced by KTPH000 wherever it would appear in captured text.
KTPH000Capture typed input linesKTPH001 can be disabled per connection entirely; commands then only appear as the server's echo in the output stream.

The prompt detection is a heuristic — a remote terminal cannot reliably know when the server disabled echo. Exotic or full-screen password prompts may not be recognized, and secrets pasted into visible commands (other than the connection's own credentials) are captured like any other text. Treat journals of sensitive sessions accordingly.

If something slipped through anyway, the viewer's KTPH000search and replaceKTPH001 removes it from the entries and the capture log after the fact. Administrators can also have korTTY redact patterns automatically — see KTPH002Enterprise policyKTPH003 below.

When a summary turned out poor, or the AI was not reachable while the journal was recorded, select the journal — or a run or group, which stands for all its journals — and choose KTPH000Re-evaluate with AI…KTPH001.
